newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Heywood sees more growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Heywood sees more growth in '97.

text.p: British building and auto products firm Heywood Williams Group Plc said on Wednesday it expected profit growth in 1997 to offset the impact of sterling's strength.
Executive chairman Ralph Hinchliffe said sterling's rise could reduce operating profits by five percent this year, but he added that the company's growth should outweigh this effect.
"I think it will just limit the upside," he told Reuters, noting that the company absorbed about 2.0 million stg of adverse currency movements in 1996.
Heywood's operating profit shot up 41 percent to 40.3 million stg in 1996, while pretax profits rose 36 percent to 39.0 million stg before exceptional items.
"I think generally it was a good year for us and we hope to build on that progress in 1997," Hinchliffe said.
"We performed almost on all cylinders, in that we had good contributions from our UK operations, our U.S. operations, and continental Europe," he added.
The company generated about 50 percent of its operating profits in the U.S. last year, with 45 percent coming from Britain and the rest from the Continent.
Hinchliffe said Heywood was not worried by the prospect of higher UK interest rates, which could weigh on demand in the housing market.

"If the economy moves forward, it's likely that we will see another half percent increase (in rates). It's one of those things which is in the background, but we're not unduly concerned by it," he said.
Hinchliffe expected most of the company's growth in 1997 to come from building products, boosted by recent improvements in its plastics extrusions operations.
He added that the company's capital spending budget would probably be roughly the same or slightly lower than last year's 14 million stg.
